name: The nominal sentence
definition: A sentence that begins with a noun. At its simplest it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar.
body: زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ (Zayd is standing), العِلْمُ نُورٌ (knowledge is light). Arabic needs no word for “is”: the two nouns side by side give the complete meaning.
In the basic sentence both parts are marfūʿ. Words such as كَانَ and إِنَّ can come before it and change the ending of one part; the books treat them after the mubtadaʾ and the khabar.
